definitions.explanation: A trip taken by a group, especially a school outing to a nearby destination.
A recreational outdoor trip, often involving walking.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}は{学校|がっこう}の{遠足|えんそく}だ。
{遠足|えんそく}のお{弁当|べんとう}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a lunch box for the school trip.

examples.japanese: {遠足|えんそく}で{動物園|どうぶつえん}に{行|い}く。
examples.english: We're going to the zoo on the school trip.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}で{遠足|えんそく}が{来週|らいしゅう}に{延期|えんき}になった。
examples.english: The school trip was postponed to next week because of rain.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちは{遠足|えんそく}をとても{楽|たの}しみにしている。
examples.english: The children are really looking forward to the school trip.

examples.japanese: {天気|てんき}がいいから{遠足|えんそく}に{行|い}こう。
examples.english: The weather is nice, so let's go on a hike.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}への{遠足|えんそく}は{気持|きも}ちがいい。
examples.english: A hike to the mountains feels great.

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}で{川|かわ}のそばまで{遠足|えんそく}に{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: We went on a family outing to the riverside.

examples.japanese: {週末|しゅうまつ}に{友達|ともだち}と{遠足|えんそく}に{行|い}って、お{弁当|べんとう}を{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I went on a hike with friends on the weekend and ate a packed lunch.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると{遠足|えんそく}{気分|きぶん}で{外|そと}に{出|で}たくなる。
examples.english: When spring comes, I get the urge to go outside like going on an outing.

notes:
USAGE: {遠足|えんそく} typically refers to school excursions for elementary and middle school students, but can also mean hiking trips.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{遠足|えんそく}に{行|い}く (to go on an excursion)
・{遠足|えんそく}の{日|ひ} (excursion day)
・{遠足|えんそく}{気分|きぶん} (excursion mood - feeling excited)

SCHOOL CONTEXT: Japanese schools often organize {遠足|えんそく} in spring and autumn to parks, zoos, or historical sites.

CULTURAL NOTE: {遠足|えんそく} evokes childhood memories and is associated with お{弁当|べんとう} (packed lunch) and {おやつ|} (snacks) that children bring.

RELATED:
・{修学旅行|しゅうがくりょこう} - school trip (longer, overnight)
・ハイキング - hiking
